cards.claim: An equation with fractional terms is simplified by multiplying both sides by the LCM of the denominators of its terms.
cards.quote: Here, we had to multiply both sides of the equation by the LCM of the denominators of the terms in the expressions of the equation.

locator.section: 2.3 Reducing Equations to Simpler Form (margin note)

cards.claim: An equation can be brought to a simpler form by opening brackets and combining like terms on both sides.
cards.quote: Note, in this example we brought the equation to a simpler form by opening brackets and combining like terms on both sides of the equation.

cards.claim: Some equations are not linear to begin with but can be brought to linear form by multiplying both sides by a suitable expression.
cards.quote: Some equations may not even be linear to begin with, but they can be brought to a linear form by multiplying both sides of the equation by a suitable expression.

cards.claim: The usual single solution fails when simplification yields a contradiction: an equation false for all values of the variable has no solution.
cards.quote: An equation that has no solution, or that is false for all values of the variable, is called a contradiction .

cards.claim: When an equation simplifies to an identity (true for any value of the variable), its solution is all real numbers rather than a single value.
cards.quote: An equation that is true for any value of the variable like this is called an identity .
